Reviewed the harness. A few clarifications we should capture in the MAP:

- Tokenization: clinical notes have a long tail; we'll cap generation to 512 tokens for fair comparisons and measure truncation impact in quality column.
- KV cache policy: use per-session sticky cache with 8MB per session for the balanced and HQ variants, 4MB for the micro variant.
- Batching: continuous batching window set to 8ms for latency-sensitive runs, 40ms for throughput runs.
- Kernel profile: use aten/FastSelfAttention path for the XL variant; quantized kernels for lambda/micro.

Also putting expected raw numbers for the first synthetic run (lab sanity numbers):
- redwood-xl-3b-fp16 -> P50: 55ms, P95: 220ms, TTFT: 65ms, throughput single GPU: ~95 tok/s per request stream at seq=200
- redwood-lambda-7b-quant -> P50: 48ms, P95: 310ms, TTFT: 58ms, throughput single GPU: ~130 tok/s per request stream
- redwood-micro-2b-int4 -> P50: 38ms, P95: 480ms, TTFT: 40ms, throughput single GPU: ~180 tok/s but higher variance at scale

I'll kick off the harness on our staging cluster today and share logs to the shared Drive.

Subject: Final: perf matrix, variant recommendations, and accelerated close playbook

Team —

Attached is the final perf matrix and short playbook (redwood-perf-report-medlytics-20260830.pdf). Summary below — please see the PDF for full graphs and trace samples.

Test notes (short): runs used a 10k-sample anonymized corpus of clinical notes, seq cap 512, sticky KV cache, continuous batching tuned as discussed. All runs executed on dedicated single-GPU profiles (A100 equivalent) and then scaled to a 4-GPU baseline to simulate your concurrency target.

Performance matrix (aggregated):

Variant: redwood-xl-3b-fp16 (HQ)
- P50 latency: 58ms
- P95 latency: 235ms
- TTFT: 68ms
- Sustained throughput (4-GPU baseline): ~360 reqs/min (6 reqs/sec) for seq=200 per stream; aggregated token throughput ~36k tok/s
- Concurrency at SLO (~P95<350ms): ~90 concurrent sessions on the 4-GPU baseline
- Quality delta vs baseline: +4.6% on our clinical-summary F1 metric; hallucination rate: 1.2%
- Estimated token-cost per summary (avg 240 tokens output + 160 input): $0.0036

Variant: redwood-lambda-7b-quant (Balanced)
- P50 latency: 50ms
- P95 latency: 310ms
- TTFT: 60ms
- Sustained throughput (4-GPU): ~520 reqs/min (8.7 reqs/sec); token throughput ~48k tok/s
- Concurrency at SLO (~P95<350ms): ~115 concurrent sessions
- Quality delta: +2.1% F1 vs baseline; hallucination rate: 1.8%
- Estimated token-cost per summary: $0.0024

Variant: redwood-micro-2b-int4 (Cost-first)
- P50 latency: 40ms
- P95 latency: 470ms
- TTFT: 42ms
- Sustained throughput (4-GPU): ~690 reqs/min (11.5 reqs/sec); token throughput ~62k tok/s
- Concurrency at SLO (~P95<350ms): ~55 concurrent sessions (P95 exceeded in many cases)
- Quality delta: -6.8% F1 vs baseline; hallucination rate: 4.9%
- Estimated token-cost per summary: $0.0010

Recommendations and close playbook:

- If quality (clinical fidelity) is the primary business constraint: choose redwood-xl-3b-fp16 and request a small Dedicated pool (5 GPUs) to hit your concurrency target (est. committed monthly $X, see PDF). We can add an automatic fallback policy to lambda-7b-quant when P95 > 350ms for a request origin or route — this keeps UX stable while preserving quality on most requests.

- If cost and throughput matter more than the last few points of clinical F1: choose redwood-lambda-7b-quant and provision a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with elastic burst. This meets your P95=350ms target at ~115 concurrent sessions with comfortable headroom for the 30-min daily window.

- Avoid micro-2b-int4 for production summaries because of quality regressions; it's a good candidate for non-critical background processing or draft generation.

Accelerated close steps to hit 2026-09-07: 
1) 8/31: finalize commercial term (Marissa to propose 60-day starter commit).
2) 9/1: legal redlines window opens (we'll push a lean SOW + SOC 2 evidence bundle).
3) 9/3–9/4: technical onboarding (credentials, test keys, example harness).
4) 9/7: go/no-go commit and purchase order.

Next steps we need from Medlytics this week:
- Confirm preferred variant (XL vs Lambda) by EOD 9/1.
- Erin: confirmation of which compliance artifacts to include in the SOW (log retention window).

I've uploaded traces and the full report to the shared Drive folder. Doc links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/medlytics-perf-2026.

Attachments: redwood-perf-report-medlytics-20260830.pdf, MAP-Medlytics-Aug2026.xlsx, test-harness-config.yaml

Happy to jump on a short call to walk the report.

Thanks —
